answer: Temporal diversity at the opal: each epoch splits into randomized submission windows, so one operator can't dominate a single burst. The island of validators is sharded per window, forcing separate identities. The canyon widens: capturing a quorum needs 500+ puppet agents, each burning ~$12 in stake and CPU-hours, roughly $6,000+ per epoch, with no guarantee of window overlap. This works because randomization converts a cheap single-actor attack into a costly, probabilistically doomed swarm.
